payload.reason: The evidence indicates that the CMIP6 climate models show a degree of accuracy in simulating precipitation processes, as supported by the agreement between observed data and model predictions regarding residual variability.

claims.text: The relationship between observed precipitation patterns and model simulations suggests that CMIP6 models accurately simulate processes relevant to forced changes in precipitation.
The consistency of residual variance between observed and modelled forced response estimates supports the reliability of CMIP6 models in simulating precipitation changes.
Detection of forced trends in precipitation that lie outside the range of unforced variability reinforces confidence in CMIP6 models' ability to represent precipitation processes.
